overview: This one-page file consists of a December 1943 acknowledgment from the State Department’s Division of Far Eastern Affairs thanking the Reverend E. Walker of Richmond, California, for donating the book “Geology of the Environs of Tokyo” to the Department’s reference collection. The letter, signed by Assistant Chief Lawrence E. Salisbury for the Secretary of State, is accompanied by brief receipt, filing, acknowledgment, and routing annotations.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of donation of “Geology of the Environs of Tokyo”
subfiles.from: Lawrence E. Salisbury, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges Walker’s donation of a geological book about the Tokyo area.
subfiles.summary: Lawrence E. Salisbury informs the Reverend E. Walker that the book “Geology of the Environs of Tokyo,” sent to the Secretary of State, has been referred to the Division of Far Eastern Affairs for acknowledgment. He expresses appreciation for Walker’s contribution to the Department’s reference materials. Administrative annotations record receipt, acknowledgment, and filing information.
keywords: Geology of the Environs of Tokyo

interest: The document provides a small but revealing example of how the State Department enlarged and tracked its reference holdings during the Second World War, including materials on the physical geography of Japan’s capital. Its receipt and filing annotations offer useful evidence about departmental recordkeeping, while the letter identifies a private individual who supplied specialist knowledge to the government.
